newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS SPOTLIGHT-HINGIS MAKES STYLISH FRENCH OPEN START.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS SPOTLIGHT-HINGIS MAKES STYLISH FRENCH OPEN START.

text.p: World number one Martina Hingis started her French Open campaign in style by crushing Slovakia's Henrieta Nagyova in straight sets on Tuesday.
Top seed Hingis, playing her first match since she hurt her left knee in a riding accident a month ago, needed just 51 minutes to outclass Nagyova 6-0 6-2 on a sunny afternoon.
The 16-year-old Swiss player looked as fit as ever, running smoothly across the court and firing astonishing winners almost at will.
Hingis appeared vaguely troubled only once in a one-sided first set, when Nagyova earned a break point in the fourth game.
But the remarkable teenager, who was already leading 3-0, saved it with a blistering forehand volley and went on to wrap up the set in 20 minutes without dropping a single game.
Nagyova, ranked 37th in the world at only 18, is regarded as a promising player but Hingis was simply in a different class.
After Nagyova won her first game of the match to lead 1-0 in the second set, Hingis won the next game to love and went on to break her opponent to lead 2-1.

Nagyova, looking helpless at times, was happy to win her serve again in the fifth game but the outcome was already way beyond doubt. A few minutes later, she hit a backhand long on match point to bow out.
"I felt I played a good match apart from a few stupid volleys," said Hingis. "I didn't know exactly what to expect but it worked out all right. It was a really good match, just what I needed."
Hingis, who took the number one spot from German Steffi Graf last March, did not even look tired as she smiled and waved to the crowd before leaving the court to loud applause.
"I was excited to go out there," she said. "It was such a great feeling to step on the court again, to see the crowd and all that. I was starting to miss it."

Hingis, who had won all her 26 matches this season before her accident and has not lost since November 1996, seems to have little to fear from her opponent in the second round, little-known Italian Gloria Pizzichini.

Even before her first match, Hingis had already won a prize in the French capital. On Monday night, she received the traditional "Prix Orange", awarded to the player considered the nicest to the fans and the press.
